The Director of Custodial and Waste Management will establish organizational direction and guide management and supervisory staff in developing and implementing organizational strategies, goals, and objectives for Custodial Services and Waste Management. Provide leadership and direction in establishing programs that ensure high-quality, cost-effective custodial, waste collection, recycling, and organics services and a strong commitment to customer service, safety, regulatory compliance, and environmental sustainability.
20% - Leadership and Communication

The operational scope encompasses the UC Davis campus and other supported locations, including facilities in surrounding areas and Aggie Square in Sacramento. Custodial Services supports more than 11 million square feet across approximately 1,200 buildings, including classrooms, laboratories, offices, research facilities, residential spaces, and other shared areas. Waste Management provides waste collection, recycling, and organics services across the supported service area.

The Director will develop short- and long-range operational plans, including annual and multiyear goals and objectives. Plan, develop, and manage an annual operating budget exceeding $20 million in General Fund and recharge funding for operations and maintenance, including the allocation, justification, control, and expenditure of funds. Develop project and equipment budget recommendations that support the maintenance and preservation of campus facilities and the safe, reliable delivery of waste management services.

The Director will establish and foster a strong customer service commitment throughout the organization and lead the resolution of significant customer and operational concerns. Oversee internal production control systems, waste and recycling service data, fleet and equipment resources, and the use of external service contracts. Ensure that waste collection, transportation, recycling, organics, and disposal operations comply with applicable federal, state, and local requirements, University policies, and campus sustainability goals. Participate as a member of the Facilities Management senior leadership team.

Provide organizational oversight for more than 200 full-time employees across Custodial Services, Waste Management, and administrative and operational support functions, including managers, supervisors, custodians, senior custodians, lead custodians, waste management staff, commercial vehicle operators, administrative staff, laborers, stores workers, and equipment repair staff.
Must possess excellent analytical and management abilities and be able to independently recommend solutions to complex problems and issues.
Substantial technical and administrative skills and knowledge to perform as a senior manager in Facilities Management, including cost management, risk management and information systems.
Skill to present complex data in a way that facilitates decision-making.
Skill to create and evaluate analytical approaches and financial models for use in resource analysis and allocation.
Skill to develop and implement safety training for a diverse work force.
Ability to develop and lead supervisors to increase efficiency, accountability, and service quality.
Knowledge and ability to provide quality customer service through effective and accepted quality methods and processes.
Skill to provide leadership in emergency situations; determine appropriate response in order to provide continuous service to campus community.
